claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first questions we need to go through.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child(ren).

**First, could you tell me:**

1. **How many children** are you wanting to claim Child Benefit for?
2. **What are their names?**
3. **How old is/are each child?** (or their dates of birth)

This will help me determine which pathway through the eligibility rules applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm wanting to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one son, **Alex, who is 18 years old**.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the **16-19 age category**. For young people in this age range, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

Let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?** (This could include school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! So Alex is in full-time education at college doing A-levels. That's helpful.

Now I need to check a few more details to ensure he meets all the eligibility requirements. Let me navigate to the next stage of checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good news - since Alex is currently in education (A-levels at college), let me proceed to the next check about the level of education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! This is a key check. A-levels are **approved education** for Child Benefit purposes. However, I need to confirm a couple more details:

1. **Is Alex studying at least 12 hours per week** with supervised study time? (This is typically the case for full-time A-level students, but I need to confirm)

2. **Is Alex working full-time** (30 hours or more per week), or working any significant hours alongside his studies?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's doing full-time A-levels, so definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study. And no, he doesn't work at all - he's focused on his studies.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex meets the education requirements - he's doing full-time A-levels (which is approved education with more than 12 hours supervised study per week) and he's not working full-time.

Let me continue checking the remaining eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great - Alex isn't working, so he definitely works less than 24 hours per week. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex receiving any of these benefits in his own right?**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (as an individual claim)

Or is he not receiving these types of benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually he does receive Universal Credit in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for clarifying that. Unfortunately, this means Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit.

Let me explain why:

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, children who are receiving **Universal Credit in their own right** are not eligible for Child Benefit. This is the case even though Alex is in approved full-time education (A-levels).

The reason for this rule is that Universal Credit provides support to young people who are supporting themselves, and Child Benefit is not paid concurrently with this type of benefit.

Let me provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

**Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Why:** Alex receives Universal Credit in his own name, which disqualifies him from Child Benefit.

**Next Steps:**

If you believe Alex's Universal Credit entitlement has changed, or if he were to stop receiving it, his eligibility for Child Benefit could potentially change. You may want to:

1. Contact HMRC to discuss your specific situation, as there may be exceptions or special circumstances
2. Monitor whether Alex's Universal Credit status changes - if he stops receiving it, he might become eligible for Child Benefit
3. Check the [GOV.UK Child Benefit eligibility page](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility) for the latest guidance

I'm sorry this wasn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

reasonings: Alex is 18 years old and in approved full-time education (A-levels at college) with more than 12 hours supervised study per week. He is not working full-time. However, Alex receives Universal Credit in his own right, which makes him ineligible for Child Benefit. The eligibility rules state that children receiving Universal Credit (or Employment and Support Allowance) in their own name cannot receive Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: Alex does not qualify for Child Benefit because he receives Universal Credit in his own name. While he meets the other criteria (being in approved education, not working full-time), the receipt of Universal Credit is a disqualifying factor."}
